metadata.notes: Recopilacion historica britanica de bebidas calientes y frias de uso en Oxford, publicada por primera vez en 1827. Incluye los clasicos britanicos del siglo XVIII y XIX: Cardinal, Pope, Lawn Sleeves, Negus en sus variantes (porto, blanco, frio), Sherbet, Lemonade, Orangeade, los varios Possets (vinosos, de cerveza, de sidra, de pera/perry, picante con pimienta), Beer Flip, Rumfustian, Cider Cup, Beer Cup, Red Cup, el Wassail Bowl o Swig de Navidad y Vispera de Reyes, y el hidromiel galos Metheglin. Documento de referencia para la coctelria pre-victoriana britanica. El OCR contiene varias erratas (LKMONADE, POSS ET, COLD WHlTE WINE) y duplicados de cabeceras y referencias bibliograficas (Howell, The English Physician, Prior) que aparecen como falsos positivos. Saltadas (no son recetas reales): Page (Linea de cabecera de pagina); Ancient Fragment. (Cita literaria, no es receta); Recipe. (Cabecera 'Recipe.', no es receta); AND POPE, (Fragmento del titulo de la siguiente seccion (CARDINAL AND POPE)); Recipe. (Cabecera 'Recipe.', no es receta); Sir Flatwood Fldchn-'1 Sack Pouet~ (Duplicado OCR-mangled de Sir Fleetwood Fletcher's Sack Posset); Prior. (Atribucion bibliografica al poeta Matthew Prior, no es receta); Recipe. (Cabecera 'Recipe.', no es receta); The English PhysiciQn. recipes.name_es: Posset de Sack de Sir Fleetwood Fletcher
recipes.method_original: Beat the yolks of twelve eggs and the whites of six very well; mix them with a pound of refined sugar and a quart of sack. Set the whole over a clear fire, stirring constantly until it becomes hot. In the meantime, boil two quarts of cream or milk; pour it gradually upon the eggs and sack from a height, stirring all the time. Cover the bowl and let it stand by the fire for two or three hours; then grate nutmeg over the top before serving.
recipes.method_es: Batir muy bien las yemas de doce huevos y las claras de seis; mezclar con una libra de azucar refinada y un cuarto de jerez. Poner la mezcla a fuego suave removiendo constantemente hasta que este caliente. Mientras tanto, hervir dos cuartos de crema o leche; verter poco a poco sobre los huevos y el jerez desde lo alto, removiendo sin parar. Cubrir el bol y dejar reposar junto al fuego durante dos o tres horas; rallar nuez moscada por encima antes de servir.

recipes.raw_text:
NEGUS.
Negus is a modern beverage, and, ac-
cording to Malone, derives its name from
its inventor, Colonel Negus. Dr. Willich, in
his " Lectures on Diet and Regimen," says,
that Negus is one of the most innocent and
wholesome species of drink; especially if
Seville oranges be added to red port wine,
instead of lemons; and drunk moderately, it
possesses considerable virtues in strength-
ening the stomach ; but, on account of the
volatile and heating oil in the orange peel,
Negus, if taken in great quantities, is more
stimulant and drying than pure wine.
                      B3

                       6
recipes.notes: Bebida inventada por el coronel Francis Negus a principios del siglo XVIII; versiones populares se hacen tambien con jerez o vino de Madeira.

recipes.method_original: Extract the juice from the peeling of one lemon, by rubbing loaf sugar on it; or cut the peeling of a lemon extremely thin, and pound it in a mortar. Cut two lemons into thin slices; four glasses of calves-feet jelly in a liquid state; small quantities of cinnamon, mace, cloves, and all-spice. Put the whole into a jug, pour one quart of boiling water upon it, cover the jug close, let it stand a quarter of an hour, and then add one bottle of boiling hot white wine. Grate half a nutmeg into it, stir it well together, sweeten it to your taste, and it is fit for use. Seville oranges are not generally used at Oxford in making Negus; when they are, one orange is allowed to each bottle of wine.
recipes.method_es: Extraer el aceite de la cáscara de un limón frotándola con azúcar en pilón; o cortar la cáscara muy fina y machacarla en un mortero. Cortar dos limones en rodajas finas; añadir cuatro copas de jalea de pata de ternera en estado líquido; pequeñas cantidades de canela, macis, clavo y pimienta de Jamaica. Poner todo en una jarra, verter encima un cuarto de galón de agua hirviendo, tapar bien la jarra y dejar reposar quince minutos. Después añadir una botella de vino blanco hirviendo. Rallar media nuez moscada, remover bien, endulzar al gusto y está listo para servir. En Oxford no suelen usarse naranjas de Sevilla en el Negus; cuando se emplean, se cuenta una naranja por botella de vino.

It is sometimes in the summer season placed in a tub of ice; when that is done it will be necessary to make the Negus somewhat sweeter, as extreme cold detracts from the sweetness of liquors.

En verano a veces se coloca la jarra en un cubo con hielo; cuando se hace así, es necesario endulzar el Negus algo más, ya que el frío extremo le quita dulzor a los licores.

recipes.method_original: In making port wine Negus, merely omit the jelly; for when port wine comes in contact with calves-feet jelly, it immediately assumes a disagreeable muddy appearance. Negus is not confined to any particular sorts of wine; if the jelly is omitted, it can be made with any, or several sorts mixed together.
recipes.method_es: Para preparar el Negus de oporto, basta con omitir la jalea de pata de ternera, ya que cuando el oporto entra en contacto con la jalea adquiere de inmediato un aspecto turbio y desagradable. El Negus no se limita a ningún tipo de vino en concreto: si se omite la jalea, puede prepararse con cualquier vino o con varios mezclados. Por lo demás, se sigue el procedimiento del Negus de vino blanco: extraer el aceite de la cáscara de limón con azúcar, añadir rodajas de limón y especias en una jarra, verter el agua hirviendo, dejar reposar quince minutos, añadir la botella de oporto bien caliente, rallar media nuez moscada, remover y endulzar al gusto.

recipes.method_original: Extract the juice from the rind of three lemons, by rubbing loaf sugar on it. The peeling of two Seville oranges and two lemons, cut extremely thin. The juice of four Seville oranges and ten lemons. Six glasses of calves-feet jelly in a liquid state. The above to be put into a jug, and stirred well together. Pour two quarts of boiling water on the mixture, cover the jug closely, and place it near the fire for a quarter of an hour. Then strain the liquid through a sieve into a punch bowl or jug, sweeten it with a bottle of capillaire. If not sufficiently sweet, add loaf sugar gradually in small quantities, or a spoonful or two of capillaire. To be served up either hot or cold. In making this Sherbet, limes are sometimes used instead of lemons, but they are by no means so wholesome.
recipes.method_es: Extraer el aceite de la cáscara de tres limones frotándola con azúcar en pilón. Añadir la cáscara de dos naranjas de Sevilla y dos limones, cortada muy fina, el zumo de cuatro naranjas de Sevilla y diez limones, y seis copas de jalea de pata de ternera en estado líquido. Poner todo en una jarra grande y remover bien. Verter encima dos cuartos de galón de agua hirviendo, tapar bien la jarra y colocarla cerca del fuego durante un cuarto de hora. Después colar el líquido por un colador fino sobre una ponchera o jarra y endulzar con una botella de jarabe de capilaria. Si no queda lo bastante dulce, añadir azúcar en pilón poco a poco, o una o dos cucharadas más de capilaria. Se sirve caliente o frío. En lugar de limones se usan a veces limas, pero no se consideran tan saludables.

SHERBET.
When e'en a bowl of punch we make,
      Four striking opposites we take ;
      The strong, the small, the sharp, the sweet,
      Together mix'd; most kindly meet;
      And when they happily unite,
      1'he bowl is pregnant with delight.

    The liquor called Punch has become so
 truly English, it is 'often supposed to be in-
 digenous to this country, though its name al
 least is oriental. The Per11ian punj, or San-
scrit pancha, i. e. 6ve; is the etymon of its
title,· and denotE:s the number of ingredients
of which it i11 composed. Addison's foa:-
/,unter, who testified so much surprise when
he found, that of the materials of which this
" truly English" beverage was made, only
the water belonged to England, would have
been more astonished had his informant also
told him, that it derived even its name from
the East.

                      9
   Various opinions are entertained respect··
ing this compound drink. Some authors
praise it as a cooling and refreshing beverage,
when drank in moderation ; others condemn
the use of it, as prejudicial to the brain and
nervous system. Dr. Cheyne, a celebrated
Scotch physician, author of" An Essay on
Long Life and Health," and who by a system
of diet and regimen reduced himself from
the enormous weight of thirty-two. stone to
nearly one third, which enabled him to liv.e
to the age of seventy-two, insists, that there
is but ·one wholesome ingredient in it, and
that is the water. Dr. Willich, on the con-
trary, asserts, that if a proper quantitr of
acid be used in making Punch, it is an ex-
cellent antiseptic, and well calculated to.
supply the place of wine in resisting putre-
faction, especially if drank cold with plenty
of sugar; it als~promotes perspiration; but
if drank hot and immoderately, it creates
acidity in the stomach, weakens the nerves,
and gives rise to complaints of the breast.

                          10
He further states, that after a heavy meal it
i& improper, as it may check digestion, and
injure the stomach•.

recipes.name_es: Posset (en verso, según Sir Fleetwood Fletcher)

ingredients.item_es: Sack (vino blanco fortificado español, tipo jerez seco)

recipes.method_original: From fam'd Barbadoes, on the western main, fetch sugar, ounces four; fetch sack from Spain a pint; and from the Eastern Indian coast nutmeg, the glory of our northern toast; o'er flaming coals let them together heat, till the all-conquering sack dissolve the sweet; o'er such another fire put eggs just ten, new-born from tread of cock and rump of hen; stir them with steady hand and conscience pricking, to see th'untimely end of ten fine chicken: from shining shelf take down the brazen skellet, a quart of milk from gentle cow will fill it; when boil'd and cold, put milk and sack to eggs, unite them firmly like the triple league, and on the fire let them together dwell till miss sing twice — you must not kiss and tell: each lad and lass take up a silver spoon, and fall on fiercely like a starv'd dragoon.
recipes.method_es: De la afamada Barbados, en el océano occidental, traed cuatro onzas de azúcar; traed de España una pinta de sack (jerez seco); y de la costa de las Indias Orientales, nuez moscada, gloria de nuestras tostadas norteñas. Sobre brasas vivas calentad sack y azúcar juntos hasta que el sack todopoderoso disuelva el dulce. Sobre otro fuego semejante, batid diez huevos recién puestos. Bajad de la repisa el cazo de bronce: un cuarto de galón de leche de vaca lo llenará. Una vez la leche hervida y fría, añadid la leche y el sack a los huevos, unidlos firmemente como la triple liga, y sobre el fuego dejadlos juntos hasta que la moza cante dos veces — y no cuentes lo demás. Que cada mozo y moza tome una cuchara de plata y se lance al posset como un dragón hambriento.

recipes.method_original: Beer flip is made the same way and with the same materials as Rum Booze, or Egg Posset, excepting that one quart of strong home-brewed beer is substituted for the wine. Beat the yolks of eight eggs with pulverized refined sugar and grated nutmeg; extract the juice from the rind of a lemon by rubbing loaf sugar on it; add the sugar, a piece of cinnamon and the beer to a clean saucepan, bring it just to the boil, then take off the fire, pour a little cold beer in and pour it gradually among the egg yolks, stirring constantly. Pour the mixture swiftly from one vessel to another until a fine white froth is obtained. A glass of gin is sometimes added, but it is better without it.
recipes.method_es: El Beer Flip se prepara con el mismo metodo e ingredientes que el Rum Booze o Egg Posset, sustituyendo un cuarto de cerveza fuerte casera por el vino. Batir las yemas de ocho huevos con azucar refinada en polvo y nuez moscada rallada; extraer el aceite de la cascara de un limon frotando azucar en pan; poner el azucar, un trozo de canela y la cerveza en un cazo limpio, llevar al hervor y retirar del fuego, anadir un poco de cerveza fria y verter poco a poco sobre las yemas, removiendo sin parar. Pasar la mezcla rapidamente de un recipiente a otro hasta obtener una espuma blanca y fina. A veces se anade un vasito de ginebra, pero es preferible sin ella. Esta bebida se sirve a los criados en Navidad y otras grandes festividades de la Iglesia.

recipes.method_original: Extract the juice from the peeling of one lemon by rubbing loaf sugar on it; cut two lemons into thin slices; the rind of one lemon cut thin; a quarter of a pound of loaf sugar; and half a pint of brandy. Put the whole into a large jug, mix it well together, and pour one quart of cold spring water upon it. Grate a nutmeg into it, add one pint of white wine and a bottle of cider, sweeten it to your taste with capillaire or sugar, put a handful of balm and the same quantity of borage in flower (Borago officinalis) into it, stalk downwards. Then put the jug containing this liquor into a tub of ice, and when it has remained there one hour it is fit for use. The balm and borage should be fresh gathered.

recipes.method_original: Put into a bowl half a pound of Lisbon sugar; pour on it one pint of warm beer; grate a nutmeg and some ginger into it; add four glasses of sherry and five additional pints of beer; stir it well; sweeten it to your taste; let it stand covered up two or three hours, then put three or four slices of bread cut thin and toasted brown into it, and it is fit for use. Sometimes a couple or three slices of lemon, and a few lumps of loaf sugar rubbed on the peeling of a lemon, are introduced. Bottle this mixture, and in a few days it may be drank in a state of effervescence. Formerly, roasted apples or crab apples were introduced instead of toasted bread, especially on Christmas-eve and Twelfth-eve, ushered in with great ceremony.
recipes.method_es: Poner en un cuenco media libra de azucar de Lisboa; verter encima una pinta de cerveza tibia; rallar nuez moscada y jengibre; anadir cuatro copas de jerez y cinco pintas mas de cerveza; remover bien; endulzar al gusto; dejar reposar tapado dos o tres horas, luego anadir tres o cuatro rebanadas finas de pan tostado y dorado. Es entonces apto para servir. A veces se incorporan dos o tres rodajas de limon y unos terrones de azucar frotados en cascara de limon. Si se embotella, en pocos dias se puede beber en estado efervescente. Antiguamente se incluian manzanas asadas o de cangrejo flotantes en lugar de pan tostado, especialmente en Nochebuena y la vispera de Reyes, presentado con gran ceremonia.

recipes.method_original: Metheglin is the pure juice of the bee, the laborious bee, the king of insects. The Druids and ancient British Bards were wont to take a carouse hereof before they entered into their speculations. It is a fermented spiced honey beverage, probably derived from the Welsh Meddyglyn (medical drink), and considered the Hydromel of the ancients. Prepare by dissolving honey in water, adding spices and herbs, and allowing to ferment with yeast. This drink always carries a kind of state with it, for it must be attended with a brown toast.
recipes.method_es: El Metheglin es el puro jugo de la abeja, la laboriosa abeja, rey de los insectos. Los druidas y antiguos bardos britanicos lo bebian antes de entrar en sus especulaciones. Es una bebida fermentada de miel especiada, probablemente derivada del galés Meddyglyn (bebida medicinal), considerada el Hidromel de los antiguos. Se prepara disolviendo miel en agua, anadiendo especias y hierbas medicinales, y dejando fermentar con levadura. Esta bebida siempre lleva consigo cierta solemnidad, pues debe acompanarse con una tostada dorada de pan moreno.
